learning_objectives: Calculate Current Ratio and Acid-Test Ratio to two decimal places
Calculate Gross Profit Margin, Profit Margin and ROCE to two decimal places
Interpret liquidity and profitability side by side and state limitations

visual_beats.directive: Income Statement card reveals five figures
Financial position card reveals four figures
Capital employed card locks at two hundred forty thousand
Liquidity and profitability labels split apart

scenes.voiceover_script: Meet Inkwell Notebook Press, which publishes pocket notebooks. One dataset drives five ratios. From its Income Statement: revenue two hundred thousand dollars, cost of sales one hundred twenty thousand, gross profit eighty thousand, expenses fifty thousand, profit thirty thousand. From its statement of financial position: current assets ninety thousand, inventory eighteen thousand, current liabilities sixty thousand, and capital employed two hundred forty thousand. Liquidity tests short-term survival; profitability tests earning power.

elements.label: Current assets divided by current liabilities
One dollar fifty per dollar owed

visual_beats.directive: Formula card slides in from the left
Ninety thousand and sixty thousand glow
Division sign flashes
Answer card reads one point five zero to one

scenes.voiceover_script: First ratio: the Current Ratio measures liquidity. Formula: current assets divided by current liabilities. Substitute ninety thousand dollars over sixty thousand dollars. Ninety divided by sixty equals one point five. The Current Ratio is one point five zero to one. Inkwell holds one dollar fifty of current assets for every dollar of short-term debt. That looks comfortable, but current assets include inventory that may not sell quickly.

elements.label: Current assets minus inventory over current liabilities

visual_beats.directive: Formula card appears with brackets
Inventory tile lifts out of the asset bar
Numerator changes to seventy-two thousand
Answer card reads one point two zero to one

scenes.voiceover_script: Second ratio: the Acid-Test Ratio is current assets minus inventories, divided by current liabilities. Substitute ninety thousand minus eighteen thousand, giving seventy-two thousand, over sixty thousand. Seventy-two divided by sixty equals one point two; the Acid-Test Ratio is one point two zero to one. This strips out stock, so it is a harsher liquidity test. Inkwell still covers each dollar of short-term debt with one dollar twenty of liquid assets.

elements.label: Forty percent green segment of sales

visual_beats.directive: Formula card shows times one hundred
Two figures glow in the fraction
Wheel fills forty percent green
Answer card locks at forty point zero zero percent

scenes.voiceover_script: Third ratio: Gross Profit Margin measures profitability. Formula: gross profit divided by revenue, times one hundred. Substitute eighty thousand over two hundred thousand, times one hundred. Eighty divided by two hundred is zero point four; the Gross Profit Margin is forty point zero zero percent. That means forty cents of every sales dollar remains after direct costs, before overheads. Compare it with the profit margin to see what overheads take.

elements.label: Forty percent bar versus fifteen percent bar

visual_beats.directive: Formula card slides into the left panel
Overhead segment eats twenty-five points
Net bar settles at fifteen percent
Answer card reads fifteen point zero zero percent

scenes.voiceover_script: Fourth ratio: Profit Margin. Formula: profit divided by revenue, times one hundred. Substitute thirty thousand over two hundred thousand, times one hundred. Thirty divided by two hundred is zero point one five; Profit Margin is fifteen point zero zero percent. Gross Profit Margin was forty percent, so overheads consumed twenty-five percentage points of sales. Because expenses are large, therefore net profit is thin, so rising rent would hurt quickly.

elements.label: Return dial turns to twelve point five

visual_beats.directive: Capital employed card shows two hundred forty thousand
Profit figure glows in numerator
Dial sweeps around to twelve point five
Answer card locks at twelve point five zero percent

scenes.voiceover_script: Fifth ratio: ROCE, return on capital employed. Formula: profit divided by capital employed, times one hundred. Capital employed is two hundred forty thousand dollars. Substitute thirty thousand over two hundred forty thousand, times one hundred. Thirty divided by two hundred forty is one eighth; ROCE is twelve point five zero percent. Every hundred dollars invested in the press earns twelve dollars fifty of profit each year.

visual_beats.directive: Three liquidity gauges settle
Three profitability bars rise side by side
Lender icon nods at liquid cover
Owner icon weighs the moderate return

scenes.voiceover_script: Place liquidity and profitability side by side. Current Ratio one point five zero, Acid-Test Ratio one point two zero: short-term cover looks sound. Gross Profit Margin forty percent, Profit Margin fifteen percent, ROCE twelve point five zero percent: the press earns steadily but not spectacularly. Because inventory is modest relative to current assets, therefore liquid cover is credible, so a lender may feel safe while an owner seeks higher returns.

visual_beats.directive: Left panel turns numbers into signals
Historic cost stamp appears on the right
Qualitative tiles fade in but stay unmeasured
Multi-year grid overlays the scene

scenes.voiceover_script: Now the limits. Ratios use historic figures and one year's snapshot; different firms use different accounting policies. They ignore non-financial factors like customer loyalty, staff skill and product quality. A good ratio cannot prove future returns. Yet ratios still turn a pile of numbers into comparable signals: liquidity for survival, profitability for efficiency. Use several years and several competitors before deciding on Inkwell.

visual_beats.directive: Five result cards line up
Liquidity pair glows green
Profitability trio glows blue
Quiz prompt appears over the balanced cards

scenes.voiceover_script: Time for a recap. Five formulas, one dataset. Liquidity: Current Ratio and Acid-Test Ratio. Profitability: Gross Profit Margin, Profit Margin and ROCE. Results: one point five zero, one point two zero, forty percent, fifteen percent and twelve point five zero percent. The question on screen asks you to interpret, not just recite. Choose the conclusion that both the profit and the liquid asset figures support.

end_of_video_recap_quiz.question: Inkwell's Profit Margin is 15.00% and its Acid-Test Ratio is 1.20:1. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: It earns profit on sales and has $1.20 of liquid assets per $1 of short-term debt
It holds no inventory at all
end_of_video_recap_quiz.visual_explanation: A profit bar marked 15.00% and a liquid-asset stack marked 1.20:1 slide together into one judgement card, while the no-inventory and cannot-cover tiles fade away.
